One configuration-composition issue found at `712c0b3`.

## Preserve existing USB denylist entries

In [`etc/tlp.d/omarchy-bluetooth-usb.conf:12`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/712c0b3eaeb1fb436a79aa6f3a349d5ce4f13d43/etc/tlp.d/omarchy-bluetooth-usb.conf#L12), `USB_DENYLIST="..."` replaces exclusions from earlier-sorting user drop-ins. TLP reads those files in lexical order, then `/etc/tlp.conf`.

The real TLP 1.10.2 parser produced this result with synthetic user configuration and an empty `/etc/tlp.conf`:

```text
50-mine.conf: USB_DENYLIST="1234:5678"
                       Effective denylist
PR uses =              seven Intel IDs only; 1234:5678 lost
Diagnostic uses +=     1234:5678 + seven Intel IDs
```

**Impact:** A device previously excluded through a numbered user drop-in can become eligible for autosuspend again after this package update. Explicit assignments in `/etc/tlp.conf` still win, as described in the PR.

**Suggested change:** Use `USB_DENYLIST+="..."` to retain earlier exclusions, and adjust the shell test's exact-syntax check accordingly. The diagnostic append variant preserved both lists while retaining `/etc/tlp.conf` precedence.

**Verified:** With synthetic USB attributes, TLP 1.10.2's device handler changed `8087:0aaa` from `power/control=auto` under defaults to `on` with this denylist. The new shell test passed.

**Documentation correction:** TLP 1.10 still supports `USB_EXCLUDE_BTUSB`, not `USB_EXCLUDE_BLUETOOTH`. The description's rationale should distinguish that existing device-class-based option from this explicit-ID approach; the two do not have identical coverage.
